New moon occurs when the Moon is between Earth and Sun and is not visible at night.
Waxing crescent is a small visible piece of the Moon becoming visible.
First quarter moon appears as a half moon and occurs about one quarter of the way around E
Waxing gibbous appears more than half lighted but less than full.
Full moon appears fully illuminated from Earth's perspective.
Waning gibbous begins shrinking after full moon, showing all but a small sliver.
Waning crescent appears as a small crescent before the next new moon.
The Moon's changing appearance is caused by its position relative to Earth and the Sun.
The Moon's phases follow a repeating cycle.
